newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea calls North's aid demand temporary impasse.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea calls North's aid demand temporary impasse.

text.p: South Korea remains hopeful North Korea will eventually accept peace talks, although its delegates are flying back to Seoul from negotiations in New York with the communist state, a foreign ministry spokesman said on Tuesday.

Lee Kyu-hyung told Reuters that discussions over a year-old proposal for four-nation peace talks hit a "temporary impasse" because North Korea set preconditions. "We regret the North did not accept the proposal but it was not a big disappointment.
"We had expected a temporary impasse to crop up any time," Lee said. "Even if the North accepts the peace talks, an unexpected variable will probably emerge."

In the past few days, senior diplomats from the United States and South Korea had tried to get North Korea's response to the peace talks aimed at securing a lasting peace to replace a fraying armistice that ended the 1950-53 Korean War. The four-party talks would also include China.
Last Wednesday, Pyongyang essentially accepted the talks proposal but then tied acceptance to demands for additional food aid and easing of U.S. trade sanctions, he said.

"Our position is clear that there should not be preconditions for the talks," Lee said. Seoul and Washington officials said working-level contacts with North Korea would continue over the peace proposal.
